newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Fire at Sunkyong Ind halts production.
newsitem.headline: Fire at Sunkyong Ind halts production.

text.p: A fire at Sunkyung Industries Ltd's factory in Suwon, outside of Seoul, halted the production of polyester filament, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"Polyester production was halted, but other factories in the complex were not affected," Kim Byung-jin said.
The fire broke out on Tuesday in the packaging section of the factory as sparks from welding work caught on to styrofoam, he said.
The packaging section collapsed in the fire and so far three people have died, he said.
Kim said it was unclear when production would resume, but would be after the building was thoroughly inspected and deemed safe.
"We are expecting some production losses, but we don't know how much it will be," said Kim.
This is the second fire in Sunkyong Industries' Suwon complex this year. An engineering plant caught fire in January with losses of about 300 million won ($335,000), he said.
Sunkyong is South Korea's second largest producer of polyester and has a monopoly on the production of acetate filament yarn.
